title: UART DMA collision STM32L4
content:
I have two concurrent UART DMA RX running in STM32l431.

 

UART2 is running all the time and UART3 is started when a command is sent and waiting for data.

 

Both of them works, but when I try to make a new DMA transfer on one of them the other stops which I do not want. Why does this happens?

scraped_replies.html:
There are two issues in your code:

1. In HW_DMA_NewUart3Rx you call HAL_DMA_Start followed by HAL_UART_Receive_DMA. The problem is that HAL_DMA_Start sets the DMA state to HAL_DMA_STATE_BUSY, so when HAL_UART_Receive_DMA tries to start the DMA internally, it gets HAL_BUSY and silently fails. Remove the explicit HAL_DMA_Start call — HAL_UART_Receive_DMA handles DMA setup internally.

2. In HW_DMA_CheckErrorflags, when any DMA error is detected, it calls HW_DMA_Init which does __HAL_RCC_DMA1_FORCE_RESET(). This resets the entire DMA1 controller including all active channels — so UART2 DMA gets killed even though it had no error. Fix the error recovery to only restart the affected channel, not the whole DMA controller.

HAL_UART_Receive_DMA tries to start the DMA internally, it gets HAL_BUSY and silently fails. .

Does it ?

Wouldn’t it return HAL_BUSY? Or another HAL error?

Sorry, I made a mistake. HAL_UART_Receive_DMA does not fail silently — it returns HAL_BUSY. This happens because the previous call to HAL_DMA_Start already set hdma->State to HAL_DMA_STATE_BUSY, so when HAL_UART_Receive_DMA tries to start the DMA internally, it sees the channel is already BUSY and returns HAL_BUSY.

Hello ​@RFlod.2 

There are a few things in your code that could be triggering this issue.

For example, in HW_DMA_CheckErrorflags(), why are you aborting both DMA channels when only one shows a problem? It would be more appropriate to abort only the DMA channel that actually caused the issue.

Also, your DMA configuration looks confusing. You configure rx2 on channel 6 with:

hdma_rx2.Instance = DMA1_Channel6;

but later you also configure DMA settings with LL code on channel 7, which does not match the previous setup.

Another point is this part:

HAL_DMA_Start(&hdma_rx3, (uint32_t)&UartHandle3.Instance->RDR, (uint32_t)databuffer, size); HAL_UART_Receive_DMA(&UartHandle3, (uint8_t *)databuffer, size);

This can be harmful because HAL_UART_Receive_DMA() already configures and starts the DMA transfer, so calling HAL_DMA_Start() first may interfere with the HAL state machine.

In general, I suggest you optimize the code and simplify the DMA handling. The issue is most likely related to the current DMA state or configuration. Try improving that part and see whether the problem disappears.
BR
Gyessine
